notes: Tests verify the skill produces valid, runnable ralphify directories (RALPH.md + scripts) from plain-English iterative task descriptions. The bundled scripts/validate.py serves as the gold-standard structural gate.

evals.prompt: I've got a Python lib (pyproject.toml, src/myapp/, tests/) sitting at 62% pytest-cov coverage and I want to grind it up to 95%. Each iteration should pick one uncovered function, write tests for it, and commit. Coverage check should run `uv run pytest --cov=src/myapp --cov-report=term-missing`. Wrap this in ralphify so I can leave it running. Project name is 'myapp'.

assertions.text: outputs/RALPH.md exists
Bundled validate.py exits 0 on RALPH.md (warnings allowed)
Frontmatter has a non-empty `agent:` field whose first token is on PATH (or is a ./script in outputs)
Body contains the literal string `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>`
Body references `{{ ralph.iteration }}` (so the agent knows where it is in the loop)
outputs/ contains run.sh (the iteration-cap wrapper the skill mandates)
Either `commands[].run` mentions pytest-cov, or a check script in outputs/ does (the user's stated probe)
Body or a check script ties the COMPLETE sentinel to a coverage threshold (mentions 95 / threshold / percent)

evals.prompt: ralphify a clippy burndown for my Rust crate. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` currently spits out 47 warnings across the workspace and I want them gone, one or two per iteration. Crate is called 'fromage-core'. Tests are `cargo test --workspace`. Conventional commits. Once clippy is clean, stop.

assertions.text: outputs/RALPH.md exists
Bundled validate.py exits 0 on RALPH.md (warnings allowed)
Frontmatter has a non-empty `agent:` field whose first token is on PATH (or is a ./script in outputs)
Body contains the literal string `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>`
Body references `{{ ralph.iteration }}` (so the agent knows where it is in the loop)
outputs/ contains run.sh (the iteration-cap wrapper the skill mandates)
`commands[].run` includes a clippy invocation (or a check script that wraps clippy)
`commands[].run` includes `cargo test` (or a script that wraps it)
Body explicitly tells the agent to use Conventional Commits format

evals.prompt: I've got a queue at `.tasks/todo-*.md`. Each one has YAML frontmatter with `state: open` or `state: done`. The body describes one porting task — moving a JS module to TypeScript. I want a ralph that picks the next open one, does the port, flips state to done, commits, and moves on. When the queue is empty, push everything and stop. Use claude as the agent.

assertions.text: outputs/RALPH.md exists
Bundled validate.py exits 0 on RALPH.md (warnings allowed)
Frontmatter has a non-empty `agent:` field whose first token is on PATH (or is a ./script in outputs)
Frontmatter agent: uses claude (the user explicitly asked for it)
Body contains the literal string `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>`
Body references `{{ ralph.iteration }}` (so the agent knows where it is in the loop)
outputs/ contains run.sh (the iteration-cap wrapper the skill mandates)
outputs/ contains a script (e.g. next-issue.sh) that surfaces the next open queue item — declared as a command
Body distinguishes the queue-empty case (push + COMPLETE) from the work case (port + flip state + commit)
Body instructs the agent to flip `state: open` -> `state: done` when an item is finished
